title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel & templates
author: Aisha Kumar
body:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and commonly used internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for managers, people-ops, finance, and engineering teams.

Scope:
- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and long-term vendors with access to Redwood systems and data.
- Excludes one-off external guests (see Guest Access procedure).

Owners and escalation paths:
- Policy owner (People Ops): Aisha Kumar (people-ops)
- Security and data owner: Marcus Chen (security)
- Procurement & finance owner: Daniel Park (finance-legal)
- Escalation: policy exceptions are reviewed by the Policy Exceptions Board (PEB) — contact people-ops@redwood.example.com

1) Access and Permissions
Purpose: Provide secure, least-privilege access to systems and data while enabling teams to move quickly.
Key principles:
- Least privilege by default.
- Role-based access where possible.
- Time-limited access for contractors and one-off needs.
- All access requests and approvals recorded in the IAM ticketing system.

Standard roles (examples):
- engineering: developer (read/write to dev envs), oncall (prod read/limited write with RBAC gates)
- infra: infra-admin (network/firewall, infra IaC ownership)
- security: security-admin (audit logging, incident response tools)
- finance: finance-read, finance-pay (billing and vendor payments)

Access request workflow (high-level):
1. Requester opens an IAM request in the internal portal, specifying justification, role, and duration.
2. Auto-approval if role matches team mapping and duration <= 7 days.
3. Manager approval required for durations > 7 days or elevated roles.
4. Security review required for any data access tagged as Sensitive or Higher.
5. Request is fulfilled by the platform team and recorded.

Periodic review:
- Quarterly role recertification: team managers must certify members' access.
- Audit: security runs quarterly audits and reports exception metrics to the leadership.

Emergency access (Break Glass):
- Procedure: designate a break-glass ticket in PagerDuty; temporary elevated access granted with mandatory 1:1 security oversight and post-mortem within 72 hours.
- Logging: all break-glass sessions are recorded and retained for 1 year.

Guest and vendor access:
- Vendors get time-bound, scoped access and must sign the Vendor Security Addendum (VSA).
- Guest access limited to non-sensitive resources; a sponsor (staff-level) is required.

2) Change Management
Purpose: Ensure safe and auditable changes to production and critical internal systems while minimizing friction for engineering.
Change categories and approvals:
- Standard changes: pre-approved routine changes (e.g., scheduled config rotations) — logged, no CAB approval required.
- Normal changes: require Change Advisory Board (CAB) review for production-impacting modifications.
- Emergency changes: implemented per Emergency Change procedure with retrospective CAB review.

Change request checklist (to be included on each change ticket):
- Change title and owner
- Impacted services and owners
- Rollout window and blackout windows
- Rollback plan and success criteria
- Monitoring and alerting to be created for the change period
- Communication plan (who to notify and channels)

CAB cadence and membership:
- Weekly CAB meeting (30 minutes). Members: representatives from eng-platform, eng-sre, security, product, and people-ops.
- Emergency CAB: ad-hoc with oncall tech leads and security.

Pre-deployment checks (production):
- Canary or staged rollout plan documented.
- Load test and smoke test artifacts attached.
- Dependency impact analysis completed.

Rollback procedure (numbered steps):
1. Trigger rollback via the deployment orchestration tool (documented rollback playbook).
2. Notify oncall and affected stakeholders.
3. Run post-rollback verification tests.
4. Create retrospective within 48 hours if rollback occurred.

3) Data Management
Purpose: Protect confidentiality, integrity, and availability of company and customer data while enabling analytics and product work.
Data classification table:
| Classification | Description | Examples | Retention 
|---|---|---|---|
| Public | Safe for public release | Marketing site copy, public blog posts | N/A 
| Internal | Company-internal, non-sensitive | Internal playbooks, roadmaps | 3 years 
| Sensitive | Internal with limited audience | Customer identifiable data (non-regulated), internal PII | 7 years or per contract 
| Regulated | Subject to legal/regulatory controls | Customer personal data under regulation (GDPR/CCPA), financial records | Per regulation/contract (see compliance)

Data handling rules:
- Encryption: All Sensitive and Regulated data must be encrypted at rest and in transit.
- Access approvals: Sensitive/Regulated data require security review and purpose-based approvals.
- Processing locations: Regulated data must be processed in approved regions as defined by compliance.
- Anonymization: Use approved anonymization or tokenization libraries before using data in analytics or ML training.

Data retention and deletion:
- Owners must maintain a retention schedule.
- Deletion requests: people-ops or security log a DSAR (data subject access request) and partner with product/eng for fulfillment.

Data breach and incident response:
- Immediately notify security@redwood.example.com and follow the Incident Response runbook.
- Legal and people-ops notified within 4 hours for breaches involving personal data.

4) Procurement and Expenses
Purpose: Provide consistent procurement and expense policies that balance speed and fiscal controls.
Procurement thresholds and approvals table:
| Spend band | Approval required | Approver | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| <= $2,500 | Single approver | Team manager | Use corporate card for subscriptions where possible |
| $2,501 - $25,000 | Two approvers | Manager + Finance | Requires PO; attach vendor quote |
| > $25,000 | Finance + Legal + Exec | Finance lead + Legal + Head of function | Requires vendor contract and C-level sign-off |

Preferred vendors and contractual requirements:
- All vendors processing sensitive or regulated data must complete a security assessment and sign the VSA.
- Use procurement portal to request new vendors; procurement will coordinate SOW and insurance checks.

Expenses policy (travel & misc):
- Use Concur for expense submissions. Receipts required for any single item > $25.
- Per diem and allowable expenses documented in the Travel section below.
- Fraud: falsified expenses trigger disciplinary action up to termination.

Invoice and payment process:
1. Vendor submits invoice to invoices@redwood.example.com with PO number.
2. Finance validates and routes for approval.
3. Payment executed on net terms agreed in contract.

5) Vendor Management
Purpose: Manage third-party risk and maintain a single inventory of vendor relationships.
Vendor lifecycle steps:
1. Intake: business owner completes vendor intake form with risk profile and data requirements.
2. Security assessment: security runs questionnaire for medium/high risk vendors.
3. Legal review: contracts and data clauses reviewed and countersigned.
4. Onboarding: vendor added to vendor registry and access scoped.
5. Ongoing monitoring: annual re-assessments for high-risk vendors.

Vendor registry fields (minimum):
- Vendor name, primary contact, business owner, services provided, data classification, contract start/end, risk rating, VSA signed (yes/no)

Termination and offboarding:
- Offboarding checklist: revoke access, collect assets, confirm data deletion or return per contract, final invoice reconciled.

6) Travel Policies
Purpose: Ensure traveler safety, cost discipline, and consistent reimbursement.
Booking rules:
- Use corporate travel portal for booking flights and hotels.
- Lowest logical fare for flights; economy for flights under 5 hours unless approved.
- Hotels: prefer approved hotels; exceptions must be justified.

Expenses and per diem:
- Domestic per diem: meals up to $75/day (receipts required).
- International per diem: determined by region (finance provides lookup table).
- Ground transportation: rideshares for local transit; rental cars only with manager pre-approval.

Safety and security:
- For travel to high-risk regions, travelers must register trip with security and complete pre-travel approval.
- Emergency contacts: security@redwood.example.com and people-ops on-call.

Travel approval flow:
1. Employee requests travel via travel portal including itinerary and business justification.
2. Manager approval required for domestic; Director+ approval required for international/high-risk regions.
3. Finance verifies estimated cost and issues pre-approval for booking.

7) Internal Templates and Forms (Appendix)
Common templates (links stored in the templates library):
- Access request template (use for IAM requests)
- Vendor intake form (procurement portal)
- Change request template (use for CAB submissions)
- Travel authorization form
- Expense report template (Concur)
- Data processing agreement checklist

Sample: Access Request Template fields (pipe-separated table for quick copy):
| requester_name | requester_email | team | role_requested | justification | duration_days | manager_approver | data_access_needed | security_approval_required |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| | | | | | | | | |

Enforcement and exceptions:
- Non-compliance: teams in breach will be notified and remediations tracked; repeated violations escalate to HR and Legal.
- Exceptions: Temporary exceptions require a formal exception request, owner, and expiry date. All exceptions documented in the Policy Exceptions Register and reviewed quarterly.

Training and communications:
- Mandatory onboarding modules: Security Basics, Data Handling, and Expense Policy — completion within 14 days of start date.
- Annual refreshers for all staff.

Review cadence:
- This document reviewed annually or after any major regulatory change. Major changes require stakeholder review and announcement to the company.
